title: Restriction and roof compatibility of cycle evaluation
statement: Let X be a scheme, T and J integer-indexed complexes of X-modules, n an integer, and e:H^n(Hom(T,J))->Hom(H^(-n)(T),H^0(J)) satisfy IsHomologyEvaluation [new-b2-homology-evaluation-definitions]. Choose opens V of X and W of V, let F be the two-step restriction defined there, and assume K=F(J) is K-injective [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Let q:L->F(T) and p:L->E be quasi-isomorphisms [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules] of complexes on the W over site. Put P=Hom(E,K), and pi its fixed (-n,0) projection [lem-sc-hom-complex-projections]. Suppose f:H^n(P)->Hom(H^(-n)(E),H^0(K)) and c:Z^n(P)->Hom(Z^(-n)(E),Z^0(K)) satisfy the two cycle factorization identities: c postcomposed by iCycles(K,0) equals iCycles(P,n) followed by pi and precomposition by iCycles(E,-n); c postcomposed by homologyπ(K,0) equals homologyπ(P,n) followed by f and precomposition by homologyπ(E,-n). Then there exist isomorphisms a from the restricted source of e to H^n(P) and b from the restricted target of e to Hom(H^(-n)(E),H^0(K)), with F(e) followed by b equal to a followed by f. There is no concentration, finite-free, support, zero-differential or IsIso(f) hypothesis.

proof.text: Use exactness of the two restrictions, the over-open equivalence, and the componentwise Hom-complex and internal-Hom comparisons to identify the restricted source and target of e with the source and target of evaluation for F(T),K. Restriction retains the local cycle characterization he. The exactness statements are the proved auxiliary moduleOverFunctor_limits_proof and moduleOverFunctor_colimits_proof in DerivedHomMayerVietoris, combined with Mathlib overFunctorEquiv and preservation of finite limits and colimits by equivalences. Do not infer projection compatibility from a bare existential Hom-complex isomorphism. Construct the degreewise comparison using the fixed product projections, overHomObjIso and the natural factor isomorphisms of internalHom_overEquiv. Restriction preserves these products sectionwise and the open equivalence preserves all limits. The product universal property gives the required projection equations, and the Hom differential formula checked after each projection gives the chain-map equations. The factor comparisons reindex local linear maps, preserving evaluation on sections.

Apply quasiIso_homComplex_map to the identity of K and each of q,p. The private helper homComplex_precomp_homology_isIso already proves the induced Hom-homology maps are isomorphisms. Compose the map induced by q with the inverse of the map induced by p to obtain a. On the evaluation targets apply the internal-Hom bifunctor to the homology isomorphisms of q,p, obtaining b. Neither construction uses invertibility of f.

Product-projection naturality shows that evaluation after precomposition by q or p agrees on cycle representatives. The first c identity identifies the evaluated K-cycle and the second identifies its K-homology class. Compare both routes after pulling back along the Hom-homology map induced by p, which is invertible. Local surjectivity of homology class maps lifts the Hom class and the source homology argument to cycles on covers; applying he and the two c identities gives equal sections there. Separatedness glues the equality, proving F(e) composed with b equals a composed with f. Zero complexes and empty opens require no additional assumption.

theorem homologyEvaluation_roof_comparison (X : Scheme.{u})
    (T J : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ) (n : ℤ)
    (e : (homComplex (R := X.sheaf) T J).homology n ⟶
      SheafOfModules.homObj (R := X.sheaf) (T.homology (-n)) (J.homology 0))
    (he : IsHomologyEvaluation X T J n e) (V : X.Opens) (W : V.toScheme.Opens)
    (hI : CochainComplex.IsKInjective ((moduleOpenOverComplexFunctor X V W).obj J))
    (E L : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules (V.toScheme.ringCatSheaf.over W)) ℤ)
    (q : L ⟶ (moduleOpenOverComplexFunctor X V W).obj T)
    (p : L ⟶ E) (hq : QuasiIso q) (hp : QuasiIso p) :
    let K := (moduleOpenOverComplexFunctor X V W).obj J
    let P := homComplex (R := V.toScheme.sheaf.over W) E K
    let π := (Classical.choose
      (homComplex_projections_exists (R := V.toScheme.sheaf.over W)))
      E K n (-n) 0 (by omega)
    ∀ (f : P.homology n ⟶ SheafOfModules.homObj (R := V.toScheme.sheaf.over W)
        (E.homology (-n)) (K.homology 0))
      (c : P.cycles n ⟶ SheafOfModules.homObj (R := V.toScheme.sheaf.over W)
        (E.cycles (-n)) (K.cycles 0)),
      c ≫ SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := V.toScheme.sheaf.over W) (𝟙 _) (K.iCycles 0) =
        P.iCycles n ≫ π ≫
          SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := V.toScheme.sheaf.over W) (E.iCycles (-n)) (𝟙 _) →
      c ≫ SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := V.toScheme.sheaf.over W) (𝟙 _) (K.homologyπ 0) =
        P.homologyπ n ≫ f ≫
          SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := V.toScheme.sheaf.over W) (E.homologyπ (-n)) (𝟙 _) →
      ∃ a : ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι).obj
          ((homComplex (R := X.sheaf) T J).homology n)).over W ≅ P.homology n,
        ∃ b : ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι).obj
          (SheafOfModules.homObj (R := X.sheaf)
            (T.homology (-n)) (J.homology 0))).over W ≅
          SheafOfModules.homObj (R := V.toScheme.sheaf.over W)
            (E.homology (-n)) (K.homology 0),
        (((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι).map e).over W) ≫ b.hom =
          a.hom ≫ f
